texts: With artificial chordae the most important thing to avoid is excessive tension when tying them: C.
A chord tied too tight or too short pulls the leaflet down into the ventricle, Hancock's string dragging it into a tent, so the leaflets no longer meet and the valve leaks or is restricted.
The new chord must restore the leaflet's natural height, tied gently at the right length, as Brook does.
Several chords are often used, and their number, spacing and attachment near the free edge are not the problem.
Memory hook: tie the new string gently; pulled too tight, it drags the leaf down.
